page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance within the e2 family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a 1/2 shared physical core of an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the shared-core architecture introduces significant resource constraints. While stress-ng single-core CPU performance registers in the average range at 2642.19, multi-core CPU performance drops to the bottom 25% with a score of 2642.78, demonstrating minimal scaling under concurrent workloads. Memory performance is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 6.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 4.83 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers.

The instance exhibits poor throughput across specialized workloads. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are in the bottom 10% at 661.0 and 682.0 respectively, while static web serving throughput is limited to 0.63 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance also rank in the bottom 10%, with Redis handling 0.82 million operations per second. However, the instance maintains basic utility for lightweight tasks, achieving 66.82 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M LLM model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-medium offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance compute or memory resources. The shared-core model allows for budget-friendly hosting of lightweight applications, development environments, and basic utility scripts, though it is not designed for production databases or high-traffic web serving.
